vocabulary.term: Determine the Whole Given the Part and Percent
vocabulary.termEs: Hallar el total dados la parte y el porcentaje
vocabulary.definition: Working backwards from a part and its percent to find the whole amount it came from.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Trabajar al revés a partir de una parte y su porcentaje para hallar el total del que proviene.
vocabulary.cloze: Working backwards from a part and its percent finds the ___.

examples.why: Dividing by the decimal undoes the multiplication.
Multiplying again makes the whole smaller than the part.

vocabulary.definition: The amount you already know — the piece of the whole that the percent describes.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La cantidad que ya conoces: el pedazo del total que describe el porcentaje.
vocabulary.visual: The $42 sale price is the part
vocabulary.cloze: How much of the base you get — your answer — is the ___.

examples.why: It is the piece of the base the percent describes.
That is the base, the whole you started from.

vocabulary.definition: The full amount the percent is measured against. The whole is always 100%.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La cantidad completa contra la que se mide el porcentaje. El total siempre es 100 %.
vocabulary.visual: The original price is the whole = 100%
vocabulary.cloze: The full amount a percent is measured against is always ___%.

examples.text: The original price a discount is taken from
examples.why: It is the 100% amount the percent refers to.
That is the part the percent describes.

vocabulary.definition: Two lines lined up — dollars on one, percents on the other — so matching marks show the same amount two ways.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Dos rectas alineadas —dólares en una y porcentajes en la otra— para que las marcas correspondientes muestren la misma cantidad de dos formas.
vocabulary.cloze: Two parallel lines pairing amounts with their percents form a ___ ___ ___.

examples.text: Dollars marked on one line and percents on the other, lined up
examples.why: Matching positions pair an amount with its percent.

examples.text: One number line with only percents on it
examples.why: With nothing to pair against, there is no second quantity.

vocabulary.definition: A math sentence with an equal sign. Here it says percent × whole = part, with the whole unknown.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una oración matemática con signo de igual. Aquí dice porcentaje × total = parte, con el total desconocido.
vocabulary.visual: 0.7v = 26,600 — the percent times the unknown whole equals the part
vocabulary.cloze: The percent number sentence is part = ___ × ___.

examples.why: Percent times whole equals part, with the unknown whole as n.
The percent relationship multiplies; it never adds.

vocabulary.definition: A ratio comparing a number to 100. To compute with it, write it in decimal form: 60% = 0.6.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una razón que compara un número con 100. Para calcular con él, escríbelo en forma decimal: 60 % = 0.6.
vocabulary.cloze: The word that means “per hundred” is ___.

examples.text: 9 out of 100 students walk to school → 9%
examples.why: The comparison is already out of 100.
That is 90%, not 9% — both terms must be scaled to 100.

copyPanel.rule: Finding the Whole Given Part & Percent
steps: 1. Identify the given part and the percentage it represents
2. Convert the percent to a decimal or fraction
3. Divide the part by the percent decimal to find the total whole (100%)

revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Puzzle Problem
revealWordProblem.text:
The percentage of each type of puzzle in a toy store before a sale is shown. During the sale, the store sold all of its 300-piece and 500-piece puzzles — 120 puzzles in all.
Question: How many of each type of puzzle did the store have before the sale?
revealWordProblem.imageAlt: A picture graph of puzzle stock by type: 300-piece 40%, 500-piece 35%, 750-piece 15%, and 1,000-piece 10%.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: The puzzles that sold were the 300-piece and 500-piece stock together: 40% + 35% = 75% of the whole stock. So 120 is 75% of the total: 0.75t = 120, giving t = 160 puzzles before the sale. Now take each percent of 160 — 300-piece: 40% of 160 = 64; 500-piece: 35% of 160 = 56; 750-piece: 15% of 160 = 24; 1,000-piece: 10% of 160 = 16. Check: 64 + 56 = 120 sold, and 64 + 56 + 24 + 16 = 160.

reviewCheck.stem: A car is now worth $26,600, which is 70% of its purchase price. What was the purchase price?
choiceFeedback: That computes 70% of $26,600 — but $26,600 is already the part.
That is not the result of any of the three methods; check your division.
hints: Which amount is the part, and which is the unknown whole?
